# Orchid reblooming

## The plants

Three moth orchids (Phalaenopsis): the white one from Tesco in Bovey Tracey, Mother's Day 2023, £12; a pink-spotted one Clare sent in a box from Valencia; and a yellow one I rescued from the reduced shelf at the garden centre for £2.50 in 2024, three roots and a prayer.

## Getting them to flower again

After the first flowering they sat there for a year producing leaves and nothing else. What finally worked, autumn 2024:

- Moved all three to the back bedroom windowsill on 1 October, which drops to 12°C at night and is about 20°C by day
- Kept that night drop for four to five weeks
- Watered every 10 days instead of weekly
- Stopped feeding during October

Flower spikes: white one 8 November 2024, pink 21 November, yellow not until 6 January 2025.

## Flowering

White one opened 14 February 2025, nine flowers on one spike. Pink one opened 2 March, two spikes, fourteen flowers. Yellow only three flowers but I was absurdly proud. Staked each spike with a 60 cm green cane and a clip when it reached 15 cm.

## After flowering

Cut the white spike back to just above the second node; it threw a side shoot and a second flush in May. Repot only every two years, in bark, in clear pots so I can see the roots go silver when they need water. Weekly routine is in [[Watering schedule]]. Tried the panel from [[Grow light buying notes]] on the yellow one; no idea yet if it helped.
